Find co-expression cliques using C++ two-level decomposition

Source: R/cliques.R
find_cliques.Rd

Finds the maximal species cliques of each hog. Then assigns the best gene to each species of the clique.

Usage

find_cliques(edges, ...)

# Default S3 method
find_cliques(
  edges,
  target_species,
  min_species = length(target_species),
  cost_weights = c(q = 1, effect = 0),
  ...
)

Arguments

edges

Data frame with columns:

gene1

Gene identifier (first gene in pair)

gene2

Gene identifier (second gene in pair)

species1

Species for gene1

species2

Species for gene2

hog

Ortholog group identifier

q_value

q-value for the edge (from pair-level testing)

effect_size

Numeric effect size

Optionally includes a type column for filtering. Pass the unfiltered table (every tested pair, e.g. the output of find_coexpressologs()): cliques are built from "conserved" rows only, but intensity fits each edge's weight scale on every row of its species pair, so a pre-filtered table changes what it measures. A table whose type column holds only "conserved" rows triggers a warning (class rcomplex_prefiltered_edges, shown once per session).

...

Additional arguments passed to the default method.

target_species

Character vector of species abbreviations.

min_species

Minimum number of species per clique (default: length(target_species)).

cost_weights

Named numeric vector with elements "q" and "effect" controlling the composite cost used for gene-assignment ranking. The cost is q * mean_q - effect * mean_effect (lower is better). Default c(q = 1, effect = 0) reproduces the original mean-q-only ranking.

Value

A data frame with one row per clique:

hog

Ortholog group identifier

One column per target species (gene ID or NA)

n_species

Number of species in the clique

mean_q

Mean q-value across present clique edges

max_q

Maximum q-value across present clique edges

mean_effect_size

Mean effect size across present edges

n_edges

Number of present edges

n_missing

Number of missing edges (always 0)

exhaustive

TRUE when the best-gene search finished within its step budget

intensity

Onnela intensity: geometric mean, across present edges, of each edge's ensemble connection probability (in (0, 1); higher = stronger conservation). Each edge's association strength (effect_size, observed overlap over its expectation) is mapped to a probability p = z w / (1 + z w), with z fitted per species pair by maximum entropy, so intensity reads as the per-edge probability that the whole clique exists. Not 1 - q_value: every clique edge already passed alpha, so 1 - q left no range (#11). Not the Jaccard index, whose null expectation grows with neighbourhood size, which ranked hub genes above equally conserved low-degree ones (#15). NA when edges has no usable effect_size column, or when any present clique edge lacks a finite value.

min_effect_size

Minimum effect size across present edges (bottleneck enrichment)

score

Sum of the present edges' score, in bits. NA when edges has no score column.

Details

The search uses Bron-Kerbosch with pivoting on the species-level adjacency graph. A backtracker picks the gene per species that minimises the mean q-value across all present edges.

The clique score adds the edge scores. Log-odds add, so the sum is the log-likelihood ratio of the conserved subnetwork (NetworkBLAST), and it grows with clique size on purpose.

The best-gene search stops after 2 million steps per species clique. A cut search keeps its best assignment so far and sets exhaustive = FALSE. Ties at the q floor go to the larger effect size, then to the gene ids first in radix order. Row order does not matter.

A group of species wired pairwise need not share one set of copies. Then it reports the largest species subsets that share one set of copies. A hog gets at most 4,096 subset searches; past that its rows have exhaustive = FALSE.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cliques <- find_cliques(edges, target_species = c("SP_A", "SP_B", "SP_C"))

# Allow partial species cliques (2 of 3 species)
partial <- find_cliques(edges, target_species, min_species = 2L)
} # }
